overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting across the observation window reveal clear viewer preference for 'What If' space scenarios and extreme planetary physics hooks. Videos employing hypothetical exploratory framing ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme visual assets (diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) capture significantly higher views-per-day and engagement ratios (likes-per-view) than straightforward declarative statements or older psychological/animal facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Space Extremes ('What If' + Extreme Asset)
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views in 5 days) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views in 9 days) strongly outperform standard declarative space facts published around the same time.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' hypothetical survival/immersion framing set in extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring colossal monetary or material scale ('$26 Nonillion Diamond Planet', 'Supersonic Rubies') consistently pull high engagement and viewer interest relative to age.
winning_patterns.action: Incorporate hyper-specific, mind-boggling numbers and rare materials into space and planetary descriptions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content regarding memory or songs stuck in your head ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', views in low double digits) shows flat performance and low engagement ratios.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia unless tied to a startling, high-stakes narrative or mystery micro-story.

weak_patterns.pattern: Short Static Declarative Facts (<15s without narrative arc)
weak_patterns.evidence: Shorter animal facts without an immersive scenario or twist ('Octopuses Have THREE Hearts', views stalling under 200 after weeks) fail to trigger sustained algorithmic momentum.
weak_patterns.action: Extend runtime toward 18-21 seconds to allow proper setup, escalation, and twist payoff.

next_video.hook_style: Hypothetical immersive danger with extreme physical consequence
next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into the Coldest Known Star (WISE 0855–0714)?
next_video.opening_direction: Start inside total pitch-black sub-zero fog where water vapor turns directly to ice crystals on your visor.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite being colder than a household freezer, its crushing gravity would instantly compress your body into a strange metallic fluid.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' space format while introducing a fresh astronomical body (sub-brown dwarf / ice star) not yet covered in previous uploads.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not mention diamond planets, TrES-2b, or J1407b
Avoid re-using diamond, ruby, or iron rain themes
Must feature a unique celestial entity outside past publishing history

experiment: Test a 21-second space 'What If' scenario focused on a sub-zero brown dwarf star, comparing its 7-day velocity against our standard diamond planet benchmarks to validate audience appetite for extreme cold versus extreme pressure.
